description: List the folders inside one Drive folder, as the options a person picks from. `parent_id` is the folder to open; omit it to start at My Drive's root. `query` keeps only folders whose name contains that text. Trashed folders are never returned. Pass `next_cursor` back as `cursor` for the next page; a null `next_cursor` ends the list. This is the browse node behind the google_drive sync picker, so its output is the scope-option shape: id, label, kind, has_children, selectable.

parent_id.description: The folder to open. Omit for My Drive's root, which Drive names "root".

query.description: Keep only folders whose name contains this text.

cursor.description: The next_cursor from the previous call. Omit for the first page.

limit.description: Folders per page, 1 to 1000. Drive defaults to 100.

query.q: built by execute.ts: trashed = false, the folder mime type, the parent, and the optional name filter

response_schema.description: files.list under the folder mime type. Lenient on purpose: Drive omits a field rather than sending null and adds fields between releases.

quirks.why_execute: Drive expresses every filter in one `q` string with its own quoting rules, so the query is built in code, exactly as google_drive-list_files-1 builds its own.
quirks.query_escaping: Drive quotes values in single quotes and escapes with a backslash, so a folder name containing an apostrophe would otherwise be a syntax error.
quirks.has_children_is_always_true: Drive cannot say whether a folder has subfolders without a second list call per folder, which would cost one request per row. So every folder reports has_children true and the picker finds an empty child page when it opens one. A cheap answer, and never a folder a person cannot open.
quirks.root_is_the_default_parent: Omitting parent_id lists My Drive's root, which Drive addresses by the literal id "root".
quirks.shared_drives: supportsAllDrives and includeItemsFromAllDrives are both always sent, so a shared-drive folder appears once the caller opens one. A shared drive's own top level is NOT under "root", so the root page shows My Drive only. Listing the shared drives themselves is drives.list, a second endpoint and a v2 of this node.
quirks.dropped_rows: An entry with no id or name is not a folder anyone can pick, so it is dropped and the rest of the page is kept.
